instructions: The night before, or at least 3 hours ahead: lay the 4 chicken thighs between two sheets of plastic wrap and pound them with a rolling pin or heavy pan until they're an even 1/2 inch thick.
Whisk the 3/4 cup buttermilk, the egg and 1 1/2 tsp of the salt in a bowl. Add the chicken, turn it so every piece is coated, cover the bowl and put it in the fridge.
On the day, grate the garlic clove into the 2/3 cup mayonnaise, stir it through and put it back in the fridge.

Pour the 3 cups oil into a heavy pot. It should be about 1 inch deep. Heat it over medium high until it reaches 350°F. No thermometer? Drop in a pinch of the coating from the next step. It's ready when it sizzles hard straight away.

Meanwhile, mix the 3/4 cup flour, 1/4 cup cornstarch, 1/4 tsp celery salt, 1/2 tsp paprika, 1/8 tsp cayenne, 1/2 tsp onion powder, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 tsp mustard powder, 1/4 tsp ginger, 1/2 tsp thyme, 1/2 tsp oregano, the last 1/2 tsp salt and the 1 1/2 tsp pepper in a shallow dish.
Drizzle 2 tbsp of the buttermilk marinade over the flour mix and rub it between your fingers until little clumps form. The clumps fry into the crunchy bits.
Finely shred a quarter of the lettuce. That should be about 2 cups. Slice 2 of the pickles thinly on an angle. Set a wire rack over a baking sheet, or line a plate with paper towels.
Lift 2 pieces of chicken out of the marinade and let the extra drip off. Press them firmly into the coating on both sides and shake off what doesn't stick.
Lower them gently into the oil, away from you. Leave them alone for 2 to 3 minutes, until the underside is golden and crunchy.

Flip them and cook the other side for 2 to 3 minutes. You're cooking them to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest one: it's done when there's no pink left. Transfer them to the rack.
Let the oil come back up to 350°F, then coat and fry the other 2 pieces the same way.
While the second batch fries, split the 4 buns and toast them cut side down in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until golden.
Spread the garlic mayo on the cut sides of the buns. Layer the lettuce, a piece of chicken and the pickles on each bottom bun and close it with the top.
advance_prep_notes: Marinate the chicken in buttermilk the night before, or at least 3 hours ahead.
method_notes: All three marinate the chicken in buttermilk, coat it in seasoned flour with cornstarch, fry it until deep golden and serve it on a toasted bun with mayo, pickles and shredded lettuce. RecipeTin Eats (the lead) adds an egg and salt to the marinade, rubs a little marinade into the coating to make crunchy clumps and fries thin pounded pieces about 2 minutes a side at 350°F, while Melissa's Southern Style Kitchen double dips through egg wash and The Modern Proper fries whole thighs at 325°F for 10 to 12 minutes. This follows the lead with thighs, which it allows, and keeps the cayenne at its mildest amount.
